questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: In the biological name Mangifera indica Linn., the abbreviation 'Linn.' written after the specific epithet indicates that:

options.text: this species was first described by Linnaeus
the genus Mangifera belongs to an order named by Linnaeus
the name is written in Latin
the plant is kept in Linnaeus's herbarium

solution.concept: Author citation in a biological name
solution.explanation: By the rules of binomial nomenclature, the name of the author appears after the specific epithet, that is, at the end of the biological name, and is written in an abbreviated form. In Mangifera indica Linn., 'Linn.' indicates that this species was first described by Linnaeus.

Linn. = the species was first described by Linnaeus

solution.final_answer: Option A: this species was first described by Linnaeus

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: In a lichen, the phycobiont is autotrophic and the mycobiont is heterotrophic.
Statement II: The association of the partners in a lichen is so close that, on seeing a lichen in nature, one would never imagine that it has two different organisms within it.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: Lichens are symbiotic, mutually useful associations between algae and fungi. The algal component is the phycobiont and the fungal component the mycobiont; they are autotrophic and heterotrophic respectively. The algae prepare food for the fungi, and the fungi provide shelter and absorb mineral nutrients and water for their partner. Their association is so close that one would never imagine that a lichen has two different organisms within it.
steps: Statement I: phycobiont = alga = autotrophic; mycobiont = fungus = heterotrophic: true
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Biological Classification', Viruses, Viroids, Prions and Lichens (lichens)
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.

questions.question_text:
Match List-I (term used for the sexual cycle of fungi) with List-II (meaning).

List-I:
A. Plasmogamy
B. Karyogamy
C. Dikaryon
D. Meiosis in the zygote

List-II:
I. Condition with two nuclei per cell (n + n)
II. Formation of haploid spores
III. Fusion of the protoplasms of two motile or non-motile gametes
IV. Fusion of two nuclei

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: A-IV, B-III, C-I, D-II
A-III, B-IV, C-II, D-I
A-I, B-IV, C-III, D-II
A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II

solution.concept: Steps of sexual reproduction in fungi
solution.explanation: The sexual cycle of fungi has three steps: fusion of protoplasms between two motile or non-motile gametes (plasmogamy), fusion of two nuclei (karyogamy) and meiosis in the zygote, resulting in haploid spores. In ascomycetes and basidiomycetes an intervening stage with two nuclei per cell (n + n) occurs; this condition is called a dikaryon.
steps: Plasmogamy = protoplasm fusion; karyogamy = nuclear fusion
Dikaryon = n + n; meiosis in zygote → haploid spores
solution.why_others_wrong: The wrong codes interchange protoplasmic and nuclear fusion, or the dikaryon with the result of meiosis.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Biological Classification', Kingdom Fungi
solution.final_answer: Option D: A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II

Chlamydomonas (a green alga) and Mucor (a fungus)
Mango and wheat
Lion and the housefly

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Which of the following spores are produced exogenously, that is, not inside a sporangium or a sac?

(a) Conidia of Aspergillus, formed on conidiophores
(b) Basidiospores of Agaricus, formed on the basidium
(c) Aplanospores of Mucor
(d) Ascospores of Neurospora
(e) Zoospores of phycomycetes

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: (a), (b) and (d) only
(b) and (c) only
(a), (c) and (e) only
(a) and (b) only

solution.concept: Exogenous and endogenous spores of fungi
solution.explanation: In phycomycetes, the asexual spores (motile zoospores or non-motile aplanospores) are produced endogenously in a sporangium. In ascomycetes, the asexual conidia are produced exogenously on special mycelium called conidiophores, while the sexual ascospores are produced endogenously in sac-like asci. In basidiomycetes, basidiospores are produced exogenously on the basidium.
solution.why_others_wrong: Any combination with (c), (d) or (e) includes a spore formed inside a sporangium or an ascus.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Biological Classification', Kingdom Fungi
solution.final_answer: Option D: (a) and (b) only

Which of the following statements are true of both Euglena and Nostoc?

(a) Both can make their own food by photosynthesis.
(b) Both have chlorophyll a.
(c) Both have a well-defined nucleus.
(d) Both have a cell wall made of cellulose.

(a) and (b) only
(a) and (c) only
(b), (d) and (e) only

solution.concept: Comparing a euglenoid with a cyanobacterium
solution.explanation: Euglena is a euglenoid protist: photosynthetic in sunlight, with pigments identical to those of higher plants; it has no cell wall but a protein-rich pellicle, and, being eukaryotic, a well-defined nucleus. Nostoc is a cyanobacterium (kingdom Monera): a photosynthetic autotroph with chlorophyll a similar to green plants, a prokaryotic cell without a well-defined nucleus, and a non-cellulosic cell wall.
steps: (b) true: Nostoc has chlorophyll a; Euglena's pigments are those of higher plants
(d) false: Euglena has a pellicle, Nostoc a non-cellulosic wall

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Which of the following features is shared by all members of kingdom Fungi and kingdom Animalia?

options.text: Their cells lack a cell wall.
Their nutrition is holozoic, by ingestion of food.
They are eukaryotic and heterotrophic.
Their body is always multicellular.

solution.explanation: Both fungi and animals are eukaryotic and heterotrophic. Fungal cells, however, have cell walls made of chitin and polysaccharides, whereas animal cells lack cell walls. Animals show holozoic nutrition (ingestion), whereas most fungi absorb soluble organic matter as saprophytes or parasites. Yeasts are unicellular, so fungi are not always multicellular.
solution.why_others_wrong: Fungi have chitinous walls, absorb rather than ingest food, and include unicellular yeasts.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Biological Classification', Kingdom Fungi; Kingdom Animalia
solution.final_answer: Option C: They are eukaryotic and heterotrophic.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: The plant body of the liverwort Marchantia is a thallus that is:

erect and radially symmetrical
differentiated into true root, stem and leaves
a creeping, branched, filamentous protonema

homosporous
isogamous
oogamous

only isogamous
isogamous, anisogamous or oogamous
absent; they reproduce only by zoospores

solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Plant Kingdom', Algae (Rhodophyceae; Table 3.1)

Pinus and Salvinia

solution.explanation: Heterospory (production of two kinds of spores, microspores and megaspores) is found in some pteridophytes, such as Selaginella and Salvinia, and in all gymnosperms, which produce haploid microspores and megaspores. Bryophytes such as Funaria, Polytrichum (mosses) and Marchantia (a liverwort) do not produce two kinds of spores.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Sexual reproduction in all algae is oogamous.
Reason (R): In Spirogyra, fusion takes place between non-flagellated gametes that are similar in size.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.concept: Kinds of sexual reproduction in algae
solution.explanation: Sexual reproduction in algae varies. Fusion of two gametes similar in size is isogamous: the gametes may be flagellated (Chlamydomonas) or non-flagellated (Spirogyra). Fusion of two gametes dissimilar in size is anisogamous (species of Eudorina). Fusion of a large, non-motile female gamete with a smaller, motile male gamete is oogamous (Volvox, Fucus). So not all algae are oogamous; Spirogyra itself is an exception.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
A plant has a free-living, photosynthetic gametophyte that bears antheridia and archegonia. Its sporophyte remains attached to the gametophyte and is differentiated into a foot, seta and capsule. Which of the following statements about this plant are correct?

(a) Its antherozoids are biflagellate.
(b) It needs water for fertilisation.
(c) Its spores are formed within the capsule after meiosis.
(d) Its sporophyte has xylem and phloem.
(e) Its zygote undergoes meiosis immediately to form spores.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: (a), (b) and (d) only
(a), (b) and (c) only
(b), (c) and (e) only
(a), (c), (d) and (e) only

solution.explanation: A dominant free-living gametophyte bearing antheridia and archegonia, with a dependent sporophyte of foot, seta and capsule, describes a bryophyte. Its antheridia produce biflagellate antherozoids, which are released into water and reach the archegonium, so water is needed for fertilisation. The zygote does not undergo reduction division immediately; it forms a multicellular sporophyte, and spores are produced within the capsule after meiosis. Bryophytes lack vascular tissue, which first appears in pteridophytes.
steps: (e) false: the zygote forms the sporophyte first
solution.why_others_wrong: Any option containing (d) or (e) includes a false statement; (a), (b) and (c) are all true, so a combination missing one of them is incomplete.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Plant Kingdom', Bryophytes
solution.final_answer: Option B: (a), (b) and (c) only

(b) and (d) only

Rhodophyceae: chlorophyll a and d with phycoerythrin; stored food floridean starch; cell wall of cellulose, pectin and polysulphate esters; flagella absent. So both have chlorophyll a and cellulose in the cell wall. Mannitol is stored by brown algae.
steps: (b) both have cellulose in the wall: true
solution.why_others_wrong: (c), (e) apply only to one of the two classes and (d) to neither.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: A plant has true roots, stem and leaves with vascular tissue but forms no seeds. Among the following, the plant is:

options.text: Selaginella
Equisetum
Pinus
Dryopteris

solution.concept: Identifying a heterosporous pteridophyte with strobili
solution.explanation: Vascular tissue without seeds indicates a pteridophyte. NCERT names Selaginella and Equisetum as pteridophytes whose sporophylls form compact strobili, and Selaginella and Salvinia as heterosporous genera whose female gametophytes are retained on the parent sporophyte. Only Selaginella has all these features.
solution.why_others_wrong: Equisetum has strobili but is not one of the heterosporous genera named. Pinus is a gymnosperm and forms seeds. Dryopteris is a fern and is neither named as forming strobili nor as heterosporous.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: In gymnosperms, the female gametophyte that bears the archegonia develops from one of the four megaspores formed by meiosis of the megaspore mother cell.
Statement II: In gymnosperms, the pollen grains develop within the megasporangia.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: The megaspore mother cell, differentiated from a cell of the nucellus, divides meiotically to form four megaspores. One of them, enclosed within the megasporangium, develops into a multicellular female gametophyte that bears two or more archegonia. The microspores develop into the highly reduced male gametophyte, the pollen grain, and the development of pollen grains takes place within the microsporangia, not the megasporangia.
steps: Statement II: false; pollen grains develop in microsporangia
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Plant Kingdom', Gymnosperms
solution.final_answer: Option C: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.

Gulmohur

options.text: thalamus
placenta
style
stigma

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: In the alternate type of phyllotaxy:

options.text: a pair of leaves arises at each node, opposite each other
more than two leaves arise at a node and form a whorl
all the leaves arise from the base of the stem
a single leaf arises at each node in an alternate manner

solution.explanation: Phyllotaxy is the pattern of arrangement of leaves on the stem or branch, usually of three types: alternate, opposite and whorled. In the alternate type, a single leaf arises at each node in an alternate manner, as in china rose, mustard and sunflower. In the opposite type, a pair of leaves arises at each node opposite each other (Calotropis, guava). If more than two leaves arise at a node and form a whorl, it is whorled (Alstonia).
steps: Whorled: more than two per node

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
A flower has the floral formula ⊕ ⚥ K(5) C(5) A5 G(2), with the stamens joined to the corolla (epipetalous) and the ovary superior. Which of the following conclusions about it are correct?

(a) The calyx is gamosepalous.
(b) The corolla is gamopetalous.
(c) The stamens are not united with one another, though they are attached to the petals.
(d) The flower is zygomorphic.
(e) The gynoecium is bicarpellary and apocarpous.

(b), (c) and (e) only
(a) and (c) only
(a), (b) and (c) only

solution.explanation: In a floral formula, ⊕ shows an actinomorphic flower and ⚥ a bisexual one. Fusion is shown by enclosing the figure in brackets, and adhesion by a line drawn above the symbols of the floral parts. K(5) means five united sepals and C(5) five united petals. A5 has no bracket, so the five stamens are free from one another; the line joining C and A shows they are attached to the petals. G(2) means two fused carpels (syncarpous). This is the floral formula of Solanaceae.

The hard layer around the seed is this endocarp, so R explains A.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements correctly compare the seed of bean with the grain of maize?

(a) Both have cotyledons in the embryo: two in bean and one (the scutellum) in maize.
(b) The mature bean seed lacks an endosperm, whereas in maize the endosperm is bulky and stores food.
(c) In both, the seed coat is fused with the fruit wall.
(d) In both, the plumule is enclosed in a sheath called the coleoptile.
(e) In both, an aleurone layer separates the endosperm from the embryo.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: (a), (b) and (c) only
(a) and (b) only
(b) and (d) only
(a) and (e) only

solution.explanation: The embryo of a dicot seed such as bean has an embryonal axis and two cotyledons; bean, gram and pea seeds have no endosperm at maturity (non-endospermous). In a maize grain, the seed coat is membranous and fused with the fruit wall; the endosperm is bulky and is separated from the embryo by the proteinaceous aleurone layer; the embryo has one large, shield-shaped cotyledon, the scutellum, and its plumule and radicle are enclosed in the coleoptile and coleorhiza.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Which of the following features is common to the flowers of the families Fabaceae, Solanaceae and Liliaceae?

options.text: Bisexual flowers with a superior ovary
Actinomorphic flowers with axile placentation
Endospermous seeds
A gamosepalous calyx with valvate aestivation

solution.explanation: In all three families the flowers are bisexual and the ovary is superior. Fabaceae flowers are zygomorphic with a monocarpellary, unilocular ovary and non-endospermous seeds, and the calyx shows imbricate aestivation. Solanaceae and Liliaceae flowers are actinomorphic with axile placentation and endospermous seeds. Liliaceae has a perianth of tepals rather than a separate calyx.
steps: Fabaceae, Solanaceae, Liliaceae: all bisexual, ovary superior
Fabaceae differs: zygomorphic, non-endospermous, imbricate calyx
solution.why_others_wrong: Fabaceae is zygomorphic and monocarpellary (no axile placentation), has non-endospermous seeds and an imbricate calyx; Liliaceae has no distinct calyx.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Morphology of Flowering Plants', Description of Some Important Families
solution.final_answer: Option A: Bisexual flowers with a superior ovary

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: In a dorsiventral leaf, the epidermis that covers both the upper (adaxial) and the lower (abaxial) surface has a conspicuous cuticle.
Statement II: In a dorsiventral leaf, it is the abaxial epidermis that may even lack stomata.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: The epidermis covers both the upper surface (adaxial epidermis) and the lower surface (abaxial epidermis) of a dorsiventral leaf and has a conspicuous cuticle. The abaxial epidermis generally bears more stomata than the adaxial epidermis; the adaxial (upper) epidermis may even lack stomata.
steps: Statement II: false; the adaxial epidermis may lack stomata
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Anatomy of Flowering Plants', Anatomy of Dicotyledonous and Monocotyledonous Plants (dorsiventral leaf)
solution.final_answer: Option C: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: The cells of parenchyma are generally:

options.text: much elongated, with pointed, needle-like apices
thickened at the corners by cellulose, hemicellulose and pectin
dead, with thick and lignified walls
isodiametric, with thin walls made of cellulose

solution.explanation: Parenchyma forms the major component within organs. Its cells are generally isodiametric; they may be spherical, oval, round, polygonal or elongated in shape. Their walls are thin and made of cellulose. They may be closely packed or have small intercellular spaces.
solution.why_others_wrong: Needle-like apices describe phloem fibres; corner thickenings describe collenchyma; dead lignified cells describe sclerenchyma.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Anatomy of Flowering Plants', The Tissues (simple tissues: parenchyma)
solution.final_answer: Option D: isodiametric, with thin walls made of cellulose

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: In a dorsiventral leaf, the vascular bundles of the vascular system can be seen in the:

options.text: palisade parenchyma only
veins and the midrib
abaxial epidermis
bulliform cells

solution.explanation: A vertical section of a dorsiventral leaf shows three main parts: epidermis, mesophyll and vascular system. The vascular system includes vascular bundles, which can be seen in the veins and the midrib. The size of the vascular bundles depends on the size of the veins.
steps: Vascular bundles lie in the veins and midrib
solution.why_others_wrong: The palisade parenchyma is part of the mesophyll; the epidermis is the covering layer; bulliform cells are modified epidermal cells of grass leaves.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Anatomy of Flowering Plants', Anatomy of Dicotyledonous and Monocotyledonous Plants (dorsiventral leaf)
solution.final_answer: Option B: veins and the midrib

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Match List-I (cell) with List-II (shape described in NCERT).

List-I:
A. Guard cells of a dicot
B. Guard cells of a grass
C. Sclereids
D. Phloem fibres

List-II:
I. Dumb-bell shaped
II. Much elongated and unbranched, with pointed, needle-like apices
III. Bean-shaped
IV. Spherical, oval or cylindrical

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

A-I, B-III, C-IV, D-II
A-III, B-I, C-II, D-IV
A-IV, B-I, C-III, D-II

solution.explanation: Each stoma has two bean-shaped guard cells; in grasses the guard cells are dumb-bell shaped. Sclereids are spherical, oval or cylindrical, highly thickened dead cells with very narrow lumen. Phloem fibres are much elongated, unbranched and have pointed, needle-like apices.
steps: Dicot guard cell → bean; grass guard cell → dumb-bell
solution.why_others_wrong: The wrong codes interchange the two kinds of guard cells, or the sclereids and fibres.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Anatomy of Flowering Plants', The Tissues; The Tissue System (epidermal tissue system)

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Collenchyma cells may assimilate food.
Reason (R): In dicotyledonous plants, collenchyma is found below the epidermis either as a homogeneous layer or in patches.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: Collenchyma cells often contain chloroplasts, and they assimilate food when they contain chloroplasts. Separately, collenchyma occurs in layers below the epidermis in dicotyledonous plants, either as a homogeneous layer or in patches. Its position does not explain its ability to assimilate food; the chloroplasts do.
steps: R: true, but about position, not the cause of A
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Anatomy of Flowering Plants', The Tissues (collenchyma)
solution.final_answer: Option B: Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The functions of a mature sieve tube element are controlled by the nucleus of a companion cell.
Reason (R): A mature sieve element possesses a peripheral cytoplasm and a large vacuole but lacks a nucleus.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.concept: Sieve tube elements and companion cells
solution.explanation: Sieve tube elements are long tube-like structures associated with companion cells. A mature sieve element possesses a peripheral cytoplasm and a large vacuole but lacks a nucleus. Because it has no nucleus of its own, its functions are controlled by the nucleus of the companion cell, which is connected to it by pit fields in their common longitudinal walls.
steps: R: true; having no nucleus is why its functions depend on the companion cell
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Anatomy of Flowering Plants', The Tissues (phloem)
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: In flowering plants, tracheids and vessels are the main water-transporting elements. In the xylem of gymnosperms, water is conducted mainly by:

options.text: vessels, as tracheids are absent
xylem fibres
tracheids, as vessels are absent
albuminous cells

solution.explanation: Xylem is composed of tracheids, vessels, xylem fibres and xylem parenchyma. In flowering plants, tracheids and vessels are the main water-transporting elements. Vessels are a characteristic feature of angiosperms; gymnosperms lack vessels in their xylem, so the tracheids conduct water.
solution.why_others_wrong: Gymnosperms lack vessels, not tracheids. Xylem fibres are supporting cells. Albuminous cells are found in the phloem of gymnosperms.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Anatomy of Flowering Plants', The Tissues (xylem)
solution.final_answer: Option C: tracheids, as vessels are absent

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Which of the following features are common to the dicot root and the monocot root?

(a) The vascular bundles are radial.
(b) A pericycle is present.
(c) There are usually more than six xylem bundles.
(d) The pith is large and well developed.
(e) The primary xylem is exarch.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: (a), (b) and (c) only
(b), (d) and (e) only
(a) and (e) only
(a), (b) and (e) only

solution.explanation: The anatomy of the monocot root is similar to that of the dicot root in many respects: it has epidermis, cortex, endodermis, pericycle, vascular bundles and pith. In roots the vascular bundles are radial and the primary xylem is exarch. They differ in that the monocot root usually has more than six xylem bundles (polyarch) and a large, well-developed pith, whereas the dicot root has two to four xylem patches and a small or inconspicuous pith.
solution.why_others_wrong: (c) and (d) apply only to the monocot root; (a) and (e) alone leave out the pericycle.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Anatomy of Flowering Plants', Anatomy of Dicotyledonous and Monocotyledonous Plants (roots)
solution.final_answer: Option D: (a), (b) and (e) only

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Match List-I (feature seen in a section) with List-II (organ).

List-I:
A. Collenchymatous hypodermis
B. Sclerenchymatous hypodermis
C. Bulliform cells along the veins
D. Usually more than six xylem bundles

List-II:
I. Monocot root
II. Dicot stem
III. Monocot stem
IV. Grass leaf

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: A-III, B-II, C-IV, D-I
A-II, B-III, C-IV, D-I
A-II, B-III, C-I, D-IV
A-IV, B-III, C-II, D-I

solution.explanation: In the dicot stem, the hypodermis consists of a few layers of collenchymatous cells; the monocot stem has a sclerenchymatous hypodermis. In grasses, certain adaxial epidermal cells along the veins are modified into large, empty, colourless bulliform cells. The monocot root usually has more than six xylem bundles (polyarch).
solution.why_others_wrong: The wrong codes swap the two kinds of hypodermis, or the grass leaf and the monocot root.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Anatomy of Flowering Plants', Anatomy of Dicotyledonous and Monocotyledonous Plants
solution.final_answer: Option B: A-II, B-III, C-IV, D-I

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
How many of the following belong to the vascular (conducting) tissue system?
phloem fibres, xylem parenchyma, pericycle, companion cells, medullary rays, tracheids, endodermis, bulliform cells

solution.explanation: The vascular system consists of the complex tissues xylem (tracheids, vessels, xylem fibres, xylem parenchyma) and phloem (sieve tube elements, companion cells, phloem parenchyma, phloem fibres). All tissues except the epidermis and vascular bundles form the ground tissue: cortex, endodermis, pericycle, pith and medullary rays. Bulliform cells are modified epidermal cells.
steps: Vascular: phloem fibres, xylem parenchyma, companion cells, tracheids = 4
solution.why_others_wrong: 3 leaves out a parenchyma or fibre component of xylem or phloem; 5 or 6 count the pericycle, medullary rays or endodermis, which are ground tissue even though they lie close to the vascular bundles.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Anatomy of Flowering Plants', The Tissue System
solution.final_answer: Option A: 4

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
A leaf section shows stomata on both surfaces, a mesophyll not differentiated into palisade and spongy parenchyma, vascular bundles of nearly similar size except in the main veins, and large, empty, colourless cells in the adaxial epidermis along the veins. Which of the following conclusions are correct?

(a) The leaf is an isobilateral leaf of a grass.
(b) When these large epidermal cells lose water and become flaccid, the leaf curls inwards.
(c) The near-similar size of the vascular bundles reflects the parallel venation of the leaf.
(d) The guard cells of its stomata are bean-shaped.
(e) Its palisade parenchyma lies adaxially.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: (a), (b) and (d) only
(a), (c) and (e) only
(b) and (c) only
(a), (b) and (c) only

solution.concept: Interpreting a section of an isobilateral leaf
solution.explanation: Stomata on both surfaces and an undifferentiated mesophyll mark an isobilateral (monocot) leaf. The large, empty, colourless adaxial cells along the veins are bulliform cells of grasses; when they are flaccid due to water stress, the leaf curls inwards to minimise water loss. The parallel venation of monocot leaves is reflected in the near-similar sizes of the vascular bundles (except in the main veins). In grasses the guard cells are dumb-bell shaped, and an isobilateral leaf has no palisade layer.
solution.why_others_wrong: (d) and (e) are false; (b) and (c) alone leave out (a).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Anatomy of Flowering Plants', Anatomy of Dicotyledonous and Monocotyledonous Plants (isobilateral leaf)
solution.final_answer: Option D: (a), (b) and (c) only

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Phloem fibres lose their protoplasm and become dead at maturity.
Reason (R): Phloem fibres are present in the primary phloem but are absent in the secondary phloem.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: Phloem fibres (bast fibres) are made up of sclerenchymatous cells. At maturity these fibres lose their protoplasm and become dead. They are generally absent in the primary phloem but are found in the secondary phloem, so R states the reverse of the NCERT position.
steps: R: false; they are absent in primary and present in secondary phloem
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Anatomy of Flowering Plants', The Tissues (phloem fibres)
solution.final_answer: Option C: A is true but R is false.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: A stem section shows conjoint vascular bundles with no cambium between the xylem and the phloem, phloem parenchyma absent from the bundles, and water-containing cavities within the bundles. The stem is most likely that of:

options.text: a dicotyledon
a monocotyledon
a gymnosperm
a dicotyledon, as the bundles are open

solution.explanation: Conjoint bundles without cambium are closed, as in monocot stems and leaves. In the monocot stem, phloem parenchyma is absent and water-containing cavities are present within the vascular bundles. Dicot stem bundles are conjoint and open, with cambium between phloem and xylem.
steps: No phloem parenchyma + water cavities → monocot stem
solution.why_others_wrong: Dicot stems have open bundles with cambium. Bundles without cambium are closed, not open. Gymnosperms are not described with closed bundles having water-containing cavities.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Anatomy of Flowering Plants', Anatomy of Dicotyledonous and Monocotyledonous Plants (monocot stem)
solution.final_answer: Option B: a monocotyledon

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: In an interphase nucleus, the nucleoprotein fibres form a loose and indistinct network called chromatin. During the different stages of cell division, cells instead show:

options.text: a larger number of nucleoli
a nuclear envelope with more pores
structured chromosomes in place of the nucleus
chromatin fibres fused with the endoplasmic reticulum

solution.explanation: The interphase nucleus (a nucleus of a cell when it is not dividing) has highly extended and elaborate nucleoprotein fibres called chromatin, nuclear matrix and one or more spherical nucleoli. During different stages of cell division, cells show structured chromosomes in place of the nucleus.
steps: Division: structured chromosomes in place of the nucleus
solution.why_others_wrong: The other options are not what NCERT describes for dividing cells; the nucleus is replaced by condensed, structured chromosomes.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Cell: The Unit of Life', Nucleus
solution.final_answer: Option C: structured chromosomes in place of the nucleus

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: In chloroplasts, the light energy essential for photosynthesis is trapped by:

options.text: the 70S ribosomes of the stroma
the circular DNA of the stroma
the enzymes of the outer membrane
chlorophyll and carotenoid pigments

solution.explanation: Chloroplasts contain chlorophyll and carotenoid pigments, which are responsible for trapping light energy essential for photosynthesis. The stroma contains enzymes for the synthesis of carbohydrates and proteins, small double-stranded circular DNA and 70S ribosomes; chlorophyll pigments are present in the thylakoids.
solution.why_others_wrong: Ribosomes, DNA and membrane enzymes do not absorb light; they serve protein synthesis, heredity and metabolism.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Cell: The Unit of Life', Plastids
solution.final_answer: Option D: chlorophyll and carotenoid pigments

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Cells vary greatly in shape; they may be disc-like, polygonal, columnar, cuboid, thread-like or even irregular. According to NCERT, the shape of a cell may vary with:

options.text: the function it performs
the number of nuclei it contains
the type of ribosomes it has
the age of the organism

solution.explanation: Cells differ greatly in size, shape and activities. They may be disc-like, polygonal, columnar, cuboid, thread like, or even irregular, and NCERT notes that the shape of the cell may vary with the function it performs. For example, nerve cells are branched and long, and red blood cells are round and biconcave.
solution.why_others_wrong: NCERT links cell shape to function, not to the number of nuclei, the ribosome type or the organism's age.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Cell: The Unit of Life', An Overview of Cell
solution.final_answer: Option A: the function it performs

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Match List-I (scientist) with List-II (year of the work as given in NCERT).

List-I:
A. Matthias Schleiden
B. Theodore Schwann
C. Rudolf Virchow

A-III, B-IV, C-II, D-I
A-I, B-IV, C-III, D-II

solution.concept: Dates in the history of the cell

In 1839 Theodore Schwann, a British zoologist, reported the thin outer layer of animal cells. Rudolf Virchow (1855) explained that cells divide and new cells are formed from pre-existing cells. questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: The two centrioles of a centrosome lie perpendicular to each other, and each has an organisation like a cartwheel.
Statement II: The centrioles of a centrosome are surrounded by amorphous pericentriolar materials.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: The centrosome is an organelle usually containing two cylindrical structures called centrioles. They are surrounded by amorphous pericentriolar materials. Both centrioles in a centrosome lie perpendicular to each other, and each has an organisation like a cartwheel.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Plasmids can confer resistance to antibiotics on some bacteria.
Reason (R): Pili are elongated tubular structures made of a special protein.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: Plasmids are small circular DNA outside the genomic DNA; they confer certain unique phenotypic characters on bacteria, one of which is resistance to antibiotics. Pili are elongated tubular structures made of a special protein, a surface structure of the cell. The composition of pili has nothing to do with how plasmids confer antibiotic resistance.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Cell: The Unit of Life', Prokaryotic Cells
solution.final_answer: Option B: Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): In a prokaryotic cell, several protein molecules can be made from a single mRNA at the same time.
Reason (R): Several ribosomes may attach to a single mRNA to form a polysome, and the ribosomes of a polysome translate the mRNA into proteins.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: In prokaryotes, ribosomes are associated with the plasma membrane. Several ribosomes may attach to a single mRNA and form a chain called a polyribosome or polysome, and the ribosomes of a polysome translate the mRNA into proteins. Because each attached ribosome translates the same mRNA, several protein molecules are made from it at once.
steps: R: true; many ribosomes on one mRNA → many proteins at once
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Cell: The Unit of Life', Prokaryotic Cells (ribosomes and inclusion bodies)
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
In which of the following does NCERT describe the presence of DNA?

(a) The matrix of a mitochondrion
(b) The stroma of a chloroplast
(c) The Golgi apparatus

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: (a), (b) and (c) only
(b), (d) and (e) only
(a) and (d) only
(a), (b) and (d) only

solution.explanation: The mitochondrial matrix possesses a single circular DNA molecule, a few RNA molecules and 70S ribosomes. The stroma of the chloroplast contains small, double-stranded circular DNA and 70S ribosomes. Plasmids are small circular DNA molecules outside the genomic DNA of bacteria. The Golgi apparatus and lysosomes are parts of the endomembrane system and contain no DNA.
solution.why_others_wrong: (c) and (e) are endomembrane components without DNA; (a) and (d) alone leave out the chloroplast.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Cell: The Unit of Life', Mitochondria; Plastids; Prokaryotic Cells
solution.final_answer: Option D: (a), (b) and (d) only

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: A gland cell synthesises and secretes large amounts of protein. Which pair of features would you expect to be prominent in it?

options.text: Abundant smooth endoplasmic reticulum and few, small nucleoli
Many microbodies and a large central vacuole
Abundant rough endoplasmic reticulum and larger, more numerous nucleoli
Abundant smooth endoplasmic reticulum and many chromoplasts

solution.explanation: The rough ER is frequently observed in cells actively involved in protein synthesis and secretion, because its ribosomes make the proteins. The nucleolus is the site of active ribosomal RNA synthesis, and larger and more numerous nucleoli are present in cells actively carrying out protein synthesis.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Match List-I (structure) with List-II (chemical composition given in NCERT).

List-I:
A. Middle lamella
B. Cell wall of a higher plant
C. Cell wall of an alga
D. Peripheral fibrils of a centriole

I. Cellulose, galactans, mannans and minerals like calcium carbonate

A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: In the membrane of human red blood cells, proteins (about 52 per cent) make up a larger share than lipids (about 40 per cent).
Statement II: In the plasma membrane, the lipids are arranged with their hydrophobic tails towards the outer sides and their polar heads towards the inner part.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.concept: Composition and arrangement of the cell membrane
solution.explanation: Biochemical investigation showed that the membrane of the human erythrocyte has approximately 52 per cent protein and 40 per cent lipids. The lipids are arranged within the membrane with the polar head towards the outer sides and the hydrophobic tails towards the inner part, which protects the non-polar tails from the aqueous environment.
steps: Statement II: false; it reverses heads and tails

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about membrane extensions and infoldings are correct?

(a) The inner membrane of the mitochondrion forms infoldings called cristae.
(b) Mesosomes are formed by extensions of the plasma membrane into the cell, in the form of vesicles, tubules and lamellae.
(c) The outer membrane of the mitochondrion forms the cristae.
(d) The tonoplast folds to form the grana of the vacuole.
(e) In cyanobacteria, membranous extensions into the cytoplasm called chromatophores contain pigments.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: (a), (b) and (c) only
(a), (b) and (e) only
(b), (d) and (e) only
(a) and (e) only

solution.explanation: The inner mitochondrial membrane forms a number of infoldings called cristae towards the matrix, which increase the surface area; the outer membrane forms the continuous limiting boundary. In prokaryotes, mesosomes are extensions of the plasma membrane into the cell as vesicles, tubules and lamellae; they also increase the surface area of the plasma membrane and its enzymatic content. In some prokaryotes such as cyanobacteria, other membranous extensions into the cytoplasm, the chromatophores, contain pigments. Grana are stacks of thylakoids in chloroplasts; the tonoplast is the vacuole membrane.
solution.why_others_wrong: (c) and (d) are false; (a) and (e) alone leave out the mesosomes.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Cell: The Unit of Life', Prokaryotic Cells; Mitochondria
solution.final_answer: Option B: (a), (b) and (e) only

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Lysosomes are formed by the process of packaging in the Golgi apparatus.
Reason (R): The Golgi apparatus receives no materials from the endoplasmic reticulum.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: Lysosomes are membrane-bound vesicular structures formed by the process of packaging in the Golgi apparatus. The Golgi apparatus is closely associated with the ER: a number of proteins synthesised by ribosomes on the endoplasmic reticulum are modified in the cisternae of the Golgi apparatus before they are released from its trans face. So R is false.
steps: R: false; ER proteins are modified in the Golgi cisternae
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Cell: The Unit of Life', Endomembrane System (Golgi apparatus, lysosomes)
solution.final_answer: Option C: A is true but R is false.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Which of the following is NOT a function of the Golgi apparatus described in NCERT?

options.text: Synthesis of lipid-like steroidal hormones in animal cells
Packaging materials to be delivered to intracellular targets or secreted outside the cell
Modifying proteins synthesised by ribosomes on the endoplasmic reticulum
Formation of glycoproteins and glycolipids

solution.concept: Functions of the Golgi apparatus and smooth ER
solution.explanation: The Golgi apparatus principally packages materials to be delivered either to intracellular targets or secreted outside the cell. Proteins synthesised by ribosomes on the ER are modified in its cisternae before release from the trans face, and it is the important site of formation of glycoproteins and glycolipids. The smooth ER is the major site of lipid synthesis; in animal cells lipid-like steroidal hormones are synthesised in the SER.
steps: Golgi: packaging, modification, glycoproteins and glycolipids
solution.why_others_wrong: The three other options are all Golgi functions listed by NCERT.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Cell: The Unit of Life', Endomembrane System
solution.final_answer: Option A: Synthesis of lipid-like steroidal hormones in animal cells

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Mesosomes help in respiration and secretion processes in a bacterial cell, which has no mitochondria.
Statement II: The pili of bacteria are made of the protein tubulin, like the microtubules of cilia.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: Prokaryotic cells have no membrane-bound organelles such as mitochondria. Mesosomes, extensions of the plasma membrane, help in cell wall formation, DNA replication and distribution to daughter cells, and also in respiration and secretion processes. Pili are elongated tubular structures made of a special protein; NCERT does not say they are made of tubulin, which forms the microtubules and centriole fibrils of eukaryotic cells.
steps: Statement II: false; pili are made of a special protein, not tubulin
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Cell: The Unit of Life', Prokaryotic Cells; Cilia and Flagella
solution.final_answer: Option C: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Which pair consists of two structures that are both NOT part of the endomembrane system and that both lack DNA?

options.text: Mitochondria and chloroplasts
Lysosomes and vacuoles
Golgi apparatus and endoplasmic reticulum
Microbodies and centrioles

solution.explanation: The endomembrane system comprises the ER, Golgi complex, lysosomes and vacuoles, whose functions are coordinated. Mitochondria, chloroplasts and peroxisomes are not part of it, and mitochondria and chloroplasts contain their own circular DNA. Microbodies (membrane-bound vesicles of enzymes) and centrioles (cylinders of tubulin fibrils) are outside the endomembrane system and contain no DNA.
solution.why_others_wrong: Mitochondria and chloroplasts contain DNA; lysosomes, vacuoles, the Golgi apparatus and the ER are all part of the endomembrane system.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Cell: The Unit of Life', Endomembrane System; Microbodies; Centrosome and Centrioles
solution.final_answer: Option D: Microbodies and centrioles

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Which of the following does NOT take place during interphase?

options.text: Replication of DNA
Condensation of chromatin into compact chromosomes
Duplication of the centriole in the cytoplasm of an animal cell
Synthesis of proteins in preparation for mitosis

solution.concept: Events of interphase and M phase
solution.explanation: Interphase consists of G1, S and G2. DNA replicates in the S phase, and in animal cells the centriole duplicates in the cytoplasm during the S phase. In G2, proteins are synthesised in preparation for mitosis while cell growth continues. Condensation of the chromosomal material into compact mitotic chromosomes marks prophase, the first stage of the M phase.
solution.why_others_wrong: DNA replication, centriole duplication and protein synthesis for mitosis all occur in interphase.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Cell Cycle and Cell Division', Cell Cycle (phases of cell cycle); M Phase (prophase)
solution.final_answer: Option B: Condensation of chromatin into compact chromosomes

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Which of the following is NOT brought about by mitosis?

options.text: Replacement of the cells of the upper layer of the epidermis and the lining of the gut
Continuous growth of plants by the apical and lateral cambium
Increase in the number of cells in a growing multicellular organism
Formation of haploid gametes from diploid cells in animals

solution.explanation: Mitosis results in diploid daughter cells with identical genetic complement. It brings about the growth of multicellular organisms, cell repair (cells of the upper layer of the epidermis, the cells of the lining of the gut and blood cells are constantly replaced) and the continuous growth of plants through divisions in the apical and lateral cambium. Haploid gametes of animals are formed from diploid cells by meiosis, during gametogenesis.
steps: Gametes from diploid cells in animals: meiosis
solution.why_others_wrong: The other three options are the roles of mitosis listed in NCERT.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Cell Cycle and Cell Division', Significance of Mitosis; Meiosis
solution.final_answer: Option D: Formation of haploid gametes from diploid cells in animals

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Electron micrographs of zygotene show that chromosome synapsis is accompanied by the formation of a complex structure called the synaptonemal complex.
Statement II: The complex formed by a pair of synapsed homologous chromosomes is called a bivalent.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: During zygotene, chromosomes start pairing together; this association is synapsis, and the paired chromosomes are homologous chromosomes. Electron micrographs of this stage indicate that synapsis is accompanied by the formation of a complex structure called the synaptonemal complex. The complex formed by a pair of synapsed homologous chromosomes is called a bivalent or a tetrad.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Cell Cycle and Cell Division', Meiosis I (prophase I: zygotene)
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Match List-I (process) with List-II (result).

List-I:
A. Mitosis in a diploid cell, followed by cytokinesis
B. Meiosis I, followed by cytokinesis
C. Meiosis II, followed by cytokinesis
D. Karyokinesis not followed by cytokinesis

List-II:
I. A tetrad of four haploid cells
II. A multinucleate condition (syncytium)
III. Two cells with the same chromosome number as the parent
IV. A dyad of cells

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II
A-IV, B-III, C-I, D-II
A-III, B-IV, C-II, D-I
A-I, B-IV, C-III, D-II

solution.explanation: Mitosis is an equational division: the daughter cells have the same chromosome number as the parent. Telophase I is followed by cytokinesis, giving a dyad of cells. At the end of meiosis II cytokinesis forms a tetrad of cells, i.e. four haploid daughter cells. When karyokinesis is not followed by cytokinesis, a multinucleate condition arises, leading to a syncytium (e.g. the liquid endosperm of coconut).
solution.why_others_wrong: The wrong codes swap the dyad and the tetrad, or the syncytium with a product of meiosis.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Cell Cycle and Cell Division', M Phase (cytokinesis); Meiosis I; Meiosis II
solution.final_answer: Option A: A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: A diploid plant cell contains 6 pg of DNA in its G1 phase. It replicates its DNA and then completes meiosis. How much DNA will be present in each of the four cells formed at the end of meiosis?

options.text: 6 pg
1.5 pg
3 pg
12 pg

solution.explanation: In the S phase the DNA content doubles (6 → 12 pg) while the chromosome number stays the same. Meiosis involves two sequential cycles of nuclear and cell division but only a single cycle of DNA replication. Meiosis I halves it to 6 pg per cell, and meiosis II, in which sister chromatids separate, halves it again to 3 pg per cell.
steps: After meiosis I: 6 pg per cell
After meiosis II: 3 pg per cell
solution.shortcut: Each gamete-like product has half the G1 (2C) content: C = 6/2 = 3 pg.
solution.why_others_wrong: 6 pg ignores the second division (or the replication); 1.5 pg halves twice without first doubling; 12 pg is the content after the S phase, before any division.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Cell Cycle and Cell Division', Cell Cycle (S phase); Meiosis
solution.final_answer: Option C: 3 pg

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): In anaphase of mitosis, as the chromatids move towards the poles, the centromere of each chromosome leads, with the arms trailing behind.
Reason (R): The chromatids are moved towards the poles by the lengthening of the microtubules attached to their kinetochores.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: At anaphase, centromeres split and the chromatids separate and move to opposite poles. As each chromosome moves away from the equatorial plate, its centromere remains directed towards the pole, at the leading edge, with the arms trailing behind. NCERT describes the sister chromatids moving towards opposite poles by the shortening, not lengthening, of the microtubules attached to the kinetochores.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Cell Cycle and Cell Division', M Phase (anaphase); Meiosis II (anaphase II)
solution.final_answer: Option C: A is true but R is false.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: In a dividing cell, the chromosomes have reached the two poles, the nuclear envelope is reassembling around each group, and a new wall is forming as a cell plate that grows from the centre outwards. This is:

options.text: an animal cell at the end of telophase, undergoing cytokinesis
a plant cell at the end of telophase, undergoing cytokinesis
a plant cell at anaphase
an animal cell at metaphase

solution.concept: Telophase and cytokinesis in plant cells
solution.explanation: At telophase, chromosomes cluster at opposite spindle poles and the nuclear envelope assembles around each cluster. In plant cells, enclosed by a relatively inextensible cell wall, cytokinesis takes place by cell wall formation that starts in the centre of the cell and grows outward to meet the existing lateral walls; it begins as a simple precursor, the cell plate. Animal cells divide their cytoplasm by a furrow in the plasma membrane.
steps: Cell plate from the centre → plant cell
solution.why_others_wrong: Animal cells do not form a cell plate; at anaphase and metaphase the nuclear envelope is not being reassembled.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Cell Cycle and Cell Division', M Phase (telophase, cytokinesis)
solution.final_answer: Option B: a plant cell at the end of telophase, undergoing cytokinesis

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Which of the following take place in meiosis II but NOT in meiosis I?

(a) Splitting of the centromere of each chromosome
(b) Separation of sister chromatids towards opposite poles
(c) Pairing of homologous chromosomes
(d) Crossing over between non-sister chromatids
(e) Attachment of microtubules from opposite poles to the kinetochores of sister chromatids

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: (a), (b) and (c) only
(b), (d) and (e) only
(a) and (e) only
(a), (b) and (e) only

solution.concept: Meiosis I and meiosis II compared
solution.explanation: In metaphase I, microtubules from opposite poles attach to the pair of homologous chromosomes, and in anaphase I the homologues separate while sister chromatids remain associated at their centromeres. In metaphase II, microtubules from opposite poles attach to the kinetochores of sister chromatids, and anaphase II begins with the simultaneous splitting of the centromere of each chromosome, so the sister chromatids move to opposite poles. Pairing (synapsis) and crossing over occur in prophase I only.
solution.why_others_wrong: (c) and (d) happen in meiosis I, not meiosis II; (a) and (e) alone leave out (b).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Cell Cycle and Cell Division', Meiosis I; Meiosis II
solution.final_answer: Option D: (a), (b) and (e) only

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Match List-I (stage of prophase I) with List-II (feature).

List-I:
A. Leptotene
B. Zygotene
C. Pachytene
D. Diplotene

List-II:
I. Can last for months or years in the oocytes of some vertebrates
II. Compaction of chromosomes continues throughout this stage
III. Longer-lived than the two stages before it; recombination nodules appear
IV. Chromosomes start pairing together (synapsis)

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: A-IV, B-II, C-III, D-I
A-II, B-IV, C-I, D-III
A-II, B-IV, C-III, D-I
A-III, B-IV, C-II, D-I

solution.explanation: In leptotene the chromosomes become gradually visible and their compaction continues throughout the stage. During zygotene chromosomes start pairing together (synapsis). The first two stages are relatively short-lived compared with pachytene, in which recombination nodules appear and crossing over occurs. In the oocytes of some vertebrates, diplotene can last for months or years.
solution.why_others_wrong: The wrong codes swap leptotene and zygotene, pachytene and diplotene, or leptotene and pachytene.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Cell Cycle and Cell Division', Meiosis I (prophase I)
solution.final_answer: Option C: A-II, B-IV, C-III, D-I

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Both mitosis and meiosis are preceded by a phase in which the DNA of the cell replicates.
Statement II: Sister chromatids separate at anaphase of mitosis and also at anaphase I of meiosis.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: Mitosis follows interphase, in which DNA replicates during the S phase. Meiosis I is initiated after the parental chromosomes have replicated to produce identical sister chromatids at the S phase; meiosis has only a single cycle of DNA replication. At anaphase of mitosis the sister chromatids separate, but at anaphase I the homologous chromosomes separate while the sister chromatids remain associated at their centromeres; sister chromatids separate only at anaphase II.
steps: Statement II: false; anaphase I separates homologues
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Cell Cycle and Cell Division', Cell Cycle; Meiosis I
solution.final_answer: Option C: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: In a culture of human cells, each cell divides about once in 24 hours, and the M phase lasts about 1 hour. Assume the cells are dividing independently and are spread evenly over all stages of the cycle. In a sample of 960 cells, about how many would be expected to be in the M phase at any moment?

solution.concept: Duration of M phase and fraction of dividing cells
solution.explanation: A typical human cell in culture divides about once every 24 hours, and the actual cell division (M phase) lasts only about an hour; interphase takes the rest. If cells are spread evenly over the cycle, the fraction found in M phase equals the fraction of time spent in it: 1/24. So 960 × 1/24 = 40 cells.
solution.shortcut: Cells in M ∝ time in M: 960/24 = 40.
solution.why_others_wrong: 24 confuses the number of hours with the number of cells; 920 is the number in interphase; 96 uses 1/10 instead of 1/24.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Cell Cycle and Cell Division', Cell Cycle (phases of cell cycle)
solution.final_answer: Option A: 40

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements comparing telophase of mitosis with telophase I of meiosis are correct?

(a) The nuclear membrane and nucleolus reappear in both.
(b) Each nucleus formed at telophase I has half the chromosome number of the parent meiocyte.
(c) Each chromosome in a telophase I nucleus still consists of two chromatids.
(d) At the end of telophase I, the chromosomes always reach the extremely extended state of an interphase nucleus.
(e) Cytokinesis after telophase I produces a tetrad of cells.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: (a), (b) and (d) only
(a), (b) and (c) only
(b), (c) and (e) only
(a) and (c) only

solution.concept: Telophase of mitosis and telophase I
solution.explanation: At telophase of mitosis the nuclear envelope assembles around each chromosome cluster and the nucleolus reappears. In telophase I the nuclear membrane and nucleolus reappear and cytokinesis follows, giving a dyad of cells. Since anaphase I separated homologous chromosomes while sister chromatids stayed together, each nucleus has half the chromosome number, and each chromosome still has two chromatids. Although the chromosomes undergo some dispersion, they do not reach the extremely extended state of the interphase nucleus. A tetrad of cells forms only after meiosis II.
solution.why_others_wrong: (d) and (e) are false; (a) and (c) alone leave out (b).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Cell Cycle and Cell Division', M Phase (telophase); Meiosis I (telophase I)
solution.final_answer: Option B: (a), (b) and (c) only

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Each daughter chromosome that moves towards a pole at anaphase of mitosis consists of a single chromatid.
Reason (R): At anaphase, the centromere of each chromosome splits and the two sister chromatids separate and move to opposite poles.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: At metaphase each chromosome is made of two sister chromatids held together by the centromere. At anaphase, centromeres split and the chromatids separate; each chromatid, now a daughter chromosome, moves to the opposite pole. Because the two chromatids of every chromosome are separated, each moving daughter chromosome has only one chromatid.
steps: R: true; splitting of centromeres and separation of chromatids is why each has one
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Cell Cycle and Cell Division', M Phase (metaphase, anaphase)
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: A graph showing the ability of chlorophyll a, chlorophyll b and the carotenoids to absorb light of different wavelengths is called the:

options.text: action spectrum
Z scheme
light saturation curve
absorption spectrum

solution.explanation: NCERT shows two graphs: one showing the absorption spectrum of chlorophyll a, b and the carotenoids (how much light of each wavelength each pigment absorbs), and another showing the action spectrum of photosynthesis (the rate of photosynthesis at different wavelengths). Comparing them shows that most photosynthesis takes place in the blue and red regions, where chlorophyll a absorbs most.
steps: Absorption of light by pigments vs wavelength = absorption spectrum
Rate of photosynthesis vs wavelength = action spectrum
solution.why_others_wrong: The action spectrum plots the rate of photosynthesis, not absorption. The Z scheme shows electron carriers on a redox scale. A light saturation curve plots rate against light intensity.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Photosynthesis in Higher Plants', How many Types of Pigments are Involved in Photosynthesis?
solution.final_answer: Option D: absorption spectrum

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Since the first product of CO₂ fixation found by Calvin was a 3-carbon acid, scientists at first searched for a CO₂ acceptor with two carbons. The acceptor they finally discovered was:

options.text: a 2-carbon compound, as predicted
a 3-carbon compound, phosphoenol pyruvate (PEP)
a 5-carbon ketose sugar, ribulose bisphosphate (RuBP)
a 4-carbon acid, oxaloacetic acid (OAA)

solution.concept: The primary acceptor of the Calvin cycle
solution.explanation: Because the first product was a C3 acid, the scientists reasoned that the primary acceptor would be a 2-carbon molecule, and they spent many years trying to identify it. Surprisingly, the acceptor molecule was a 5-carbon ketose sugar, ribulose bisphosphate (RuBP); CO₂ (1 C) + RuBP (5 C) gives two molecules of 3-PGA.
solution.why_others_wrong: No 2-carbon acceptor was found. PEP is the primary acceptor of the C4 pathway in mesophyll cells, and OAA is the first product of the C4 pathway.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Photosynthesis in Higher Plants', The Primary Acceptor of CO₂
solution.final_answer: Option C: a 5-carbon ketose sugar, ribulose bisphosphate (RuBP)

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Match List-I (process) with List-II (product(s)).

List-I:
A. Non-cyclic photophosphorylation
B. Cyclic photophosphorylation
C. Carboxylation of RuBP by RuBisCO with CO₂
D. Combination of RuBP with O₂

List-II:
I. Two molecules of 3-PGA
II. One molecule of PGA and one of phosphoglycolate
III. ATP, NADPH + H⁺ and O₂
IV. ATP only

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: A-IV, B-III, C-I, D-II
A-III, B-IV, C-II, D-I
A-I, B-IV, C-III, D-II
A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II

solution.concept: Products of the reactions of photosynthesis
solution.explanation: In non-cyclic photophosphorylation both ATP and NADPH + H⁺ are synthesised, and O₂ is released by the splitting of water. Cyclic photophosphorylation results in the synthesis of ATP only, not NADPH + H⁺. RuBisCO carboxylates RuBP with CO₂ to form two molecules of 3-PGA. In photorespiration, RuBP combines with O₂ to form one molecule of PGA and phosphoglycolate.
solution.why_others_wrong: The wrong codes swap the two kinds of photophosphorylation, or the carboxylation and oxygenation products.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Photosynthesis in Higher Plants', Cyclic and Non-cyclic Photo-phosphorylation; The Calvin Cycle; Photorespiration
solution.final_answer: Option D: A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: The splitting of water associated with Photosystem II releases:

options.text: CO₂ and electrons
protons (H⁺), electrons and O₂
ATP and NADPH
O₂ and NADPH only

solution.explanation: Electrons removed from PS II are replaced by electrons available from the splitting of water: 2H₂O → 4H⁺ + O₂ + 4e⁻. The water-splitting complex is associated with PS II. The electrons replace those lost by PS II, the protons accumulate in the lumen, and oxygen is released as a by-product.
solution.why_others_wrong: CO₂ is not produced by the light reaction. ATP is made by ATP synthase and NADPH by NADP reductase, not directly by water splitting.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Photosynthesis in Higher Plants', The Electron Transport (splitting of water)
solution.final_answer: Option B: protons (H⁺), electrons and O₂

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Water is split in the light reaction as 2H₂O → 4H⁺ + O₂ + 4e⁻. The electrons are finally passed to NADP⁺, each molecule of NADP⁺ accepting two electrons to form NADPH + H⁺. If 6 molecules of water are split, how many molecules of NADPH can be formed?

solution.explanation: Every 2 molecules of water give 4 electrons, so 6 molecules give 12 electrons (and 3 O₂). Each NADP⁺ needs two electrons to be reduced to NADPH + H⁺, so 12 electrons reduce 6 NADP⁺. In other words, one NADPH is formed for every molecule of water split.
solution.shortcut: One NADPH per water molecule split.
solution.why_others_wrong: 3 is the number of O₂ molecules; 12 is the number of electrons (or protons); 24 multiplies the electrons by two instead of dividing.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Photosynthesis in Higher Plants', The Electron Transport (splitting of water; NADP⁺ reduction)
solution.final_answer: Option D: 6

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Chlorophyll a is the chief pigment associated with photosynthesis.
Reason (R): On a paper chromatogram of leaf pigments, xanthophylls appear yellow.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: Chlorophyll a (bright or blue-green on a chromatogram) is the chief pigment associated with photosynthesis; it forms the reaction centres of both photosystems. Chlorophyll b (yellow-green), xanthophylls (yellow) and carotenoids (yellow to yellow-orange) are accessory pigments. The colour of xanthophylls on a chromatogram has nothing to do with why chlorophyll a is the chief pigment.
steps: R is about a different pigment's colour
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Photosynthesis in Higher Plants', How many Types of Pigments are Involved in Photosynthesis?
solution.final_answer: Option B: Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The regeneration of RuBP in the Calvin cycle requires ATP.
Reason (R): The regeneration of RuBP in the Calvin cycle requires NADPH.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.concept: Energy needs of the stages of the Calvin cycle
solution.explanation: The reduction stage uses 2 molecules of ATP for phosphorylation and 2 of NADPH for reduction per CO₂ fixed. The regeneration of the CO₂ acceptor RuBP requires one ATP for phosphorylation to form RuBP; it does not use NADPH.
steps: R: false; NADPH is used only in reduction
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Photosynthesis in Higher Plants', The Calvin Cycle (regeneration)
solution.final_answer: Option C: A is true but R is false.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Which of the following take place in the stroma of the chloroplast?

(a) Carboxylation of RuBP by RuBisCO
(b) Reduction of PGA to carbohydrate using ATP and NADPH
(c) Regeneration of RuBP
(d) Splitting of water
(e) Diffusion of protons through the CF₀ channel of ATP synthase

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: (a), (b) and (d) only
(a), (b) and (c) only
(b), (c) and (e) only
(a) and (c) only

solution.concept: Sites of reactions in the chloroplast
solution.explanation: The membrane system (thylakoids) traps light energy and synthesises ATP and NADPH; the enzymatic reactions that incorporate CO₂ into sugar take place in the stroma. So carboxylation, reduction and regeneration of the Calvin cycle occur in the stroma. Water is split on the inner (lumen) side of the thylakoid membrane, and protons pass through the CF₀ channel, which is embedded in the thylakoid membrane.
solution.why_others_wrong: (d) and (e) are thylakoid membrane events; (a) and (c) alone leave out reduction.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Photosynthesis in Higher Plants', Where does Photosynthesis take place?; The Calvin Cycle; The Chemiosmotic Hypothesis
solution.final_answer: Option B: (a), (b) and (c) only

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Match List-I (factor) with List-II (NCERT's statement about it).

List-I:
A. Light
B. Carbon dioxide
C. Temperature
D. Water

List-II:
I. The dark reactions, being enzymatic, are controlled by it
II. Its stress causes stomata to close and leaves to wilt
III. Saturation occurs at about 10 per cent of full sunlight
IV. The major limiting factor; present in the atmosphere at 0.03–0.04 per cent

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II
A-IV, B-III, C-I, D-II
A-III, B-IV, C-II, D-I
A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II

solution.explanation: Light saturation occurs at about 10 per cent of full sunlight, so light is rarely limiting except in shade or dense forests. Carbon dioxide is the major limiting factor; its atmospheric concentration is very low, 0.03–0.04 per cent. The dark reactions, being enzymatic, are temperature controlled. Water stress causes the stomata to close, reducing CO₂ availability, and makes leaves wilt.
solution.why_others_wrong: The wrong codes swap light and CO₂, temperature and water, or CO₂ and temperature.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Photosynthesis in Higher Plants', Factors affecting Photosynthesis
